title: A novel in silico approach for identifying multi-target JAK/STAT inhibitors as anticancer agents.
authors: Bono, Alessia; La Monica, Gabriele; Alamia, Federica; Lauria, Antonino; Martorana, Annamaria
one_liner_zh: 该文用虚拟筛选、分子对接和MD寻找JAK/STAT小分子抑制剂，对象为蛋白-小分子而非蛋白-DNA互作，仅方法可部分借鉴，与TF-DNA课题关系疏远。
abstract: Apoptosis, or programmed cell death, plays a pivotal role in maintaining cellular homeostasis by eliminating damaged or surplus cells. Dysregulation of signaling pathways, such as JAK/STAT, is implicated in various diseases, rendering them attractive therapeutic targets for potential new anticancer drugs. Concurrently, it is imperative to preserve essential proteins like TNF-alpha and p53 to maintain normal cellular life/death balance. In light of these considerations, this study employs an innovative in silico hybrid and hierarchical virtual screening approach aimed at identifying JAK/STAT multi-target inhibitors as potential anticancer agents for several tumoral diseases. Initially, the Biotarget Predictor Tool is utilized in a combined ON/OFF-target/Multitarget mode using the extensive National Cancer Institute (NCI) database, previously filtered by ADME evaluation tools. Subsequently, Molecular Docking studies are conducted on JAK2, JAK3, and STAT3, facilitating the identification of the most promising compound, 755435. Finally, Molecular Dynamics Simulations validate the high stability of the potential multitarget inhibitor 755435 in complex with JAK2, JAK3, and STAT3.
abstract_zh: 细胞凋亡（apoptosis），即程序性细胞死亡，在维持细胞稳态中发挥关键作用，通过清除受损或多余细胞实现。信号通路（如JAK/STAT）的失调与多种疾病相关，使其成为潜在新型抗癌药物的有吸引力的治疗靶点。同时，必须保留TNF-alpha和p53等必需蛋白，以维持正常的细胞生死平衡。鉴于这些考虑，本研究采用一种创新的计算机模拟混合分层虚拟筛选方法，旨在识别JAK/STAT多靶点抑制剂，作为多种肿瘤疾病的潜在抗癌药物。首先，利用生物靶点预测工具（Biotarget Predictor Tool），结合ON/OFF靶点/多靶点模式，使用先前经ADME评估工具过滤的广泛国家癌症研究所（NCI）数据库。随后，对JAK2、JAK3和STAT3进行分子对接（Molecular Docking）研究，以识别最有前景的化合物755435。最后，分子动力学模拟（Molecular Dynamics Simulations）验证了潜在多靶点抑制剂755435与JAK2、JAK3和STAT3复合物的高稳定性。
